{{Elections in New Mexico}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in New Mexico''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[New Mexico]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Ben Ray Luján]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former oil and gas operator Larry Marker.

[[Primary election]]s were held on June 2. Luján won the Democratic nomination with 83.7% of the vote against minimal opposition. After no Republicans qualified for the primary ballot, Marker was nominated as a write-in candidate.

Republicans have not won a Senate election in New Mexico since [[2002 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2002]].

== Democratic primary ==
[[Ben Ray Luján]], a member of the Luján political family, was elected in [[2020 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2020]] after serving as the representative for the [[New Mexico's 3rd congressional district|3rd congressional district]] from 2009 until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yachnin |first=Jennifer |date=2015-06-26 |title=In New Mexico, it's good to be a Luján |url=https://www.eenews.net/articles/in-new-mexico-its-good-to-be-a-lujan/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=E&E News by POLITICO |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=LUJÁN, Ben Ray {{!}} US House of Representatives: History, Art & Archives |url=https://history.house.gov/People/Listing/L/LUJAN,-Ben-Ray-(L000570)/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=history.house.gov |language=en}}</ref> During his tenure in the Senate, Luján has been an outspoken critic of [[Donald Trump]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Mexico congressional delegation lambasts Trump's threats against Iran • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/briefs/new-mexico-congressional-delegation-members-lambast-trumps-threats-against-iran/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Pat |date=2026-01-26 |title=New Mexico's Heinrich, Luján pledge 'NO' votes on ICE funding, risking partial shutdown |url=https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2026/01/26/new-mexicos-heinrich-lujan-pledge-no-votes-on-ice-funding-risking-partial-shutdown/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=New Mexico Political Report |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Patrick |date=2026-02-25 |title=NM Democrat says President Trump was "lying to the American people" in State of the Union |url=https://www.ksfr.org/government/2026-02-25/nm-democrat-says-president-trump-was-lying-to-the-american-people-in-state-of-the-union |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=KSFR |language=en}}</ref> having voted in line with Trump's stated position only 5% of the time.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-03-07 |title=How often do New Mexico's Senators and Reps vote with Trump? A new report tallies the results. |url=https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2026/03/07/how-often-do-new-mexicos-senators-and-reps-vote-with-trump-a-new-report-tallies-the-results/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=New Mexico Political Report |language=en-US}}</ref> Luján was widely considered the favorite in the primary election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coleman |first=J. Miles |date=2026-02-20 |title=Come On and Take a Free Ride: Looking Back at “Uncontested” Senate Races |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/come-on-and-take-a-free-ride-looking-back-at-uncontested-senate-races/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Luján's sole opponent in the primary is Matt Dodson, a [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] veteran from [[Farmington, New Mexico|Farmington]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Towne |first=Robert |date=2026-02-17 |title=No Republican will challenge US Sen. Ben Ray Luján for reelection |url=https://www.kob.com/news/top-news/no-republican-will-challenge-senator-ben-ray-lujan-for-reelection/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=KOB.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> A self-described [[Democratic socialism|democratic socialist]], Dodson had previously ran unsuccessfully for local and state offices.<ref name=":0" /> Originally failing to achieve the 20% threshold of votes in the Democratic Party convention, he qualified for the ballot through signature collection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowling |first=Joshua |date=2026-03-25 |title=NM election officials qualify most statewide candidates for June 2 primary ballot • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/2026/03/25/nm-election-officials-qualify-most-statewide-candidates-for-june-primary-ballot/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}</ref>

Dodson is currently suspended from the state Democratic Party, and had previously accused [[San Juan County, New Mexico|San Juan County]] party chair Mary Schildmeyer of embezzling funds. He denied the allegations, and charges were dropped due to lack of evidence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowling |first=Joshua |last2=Lohmann |first2=Patrick |last3=Prokop |first3=Danielle |date=2026-04-03 |title=New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/2026/04/03/new-mexico-election-2026-trail-notes-7/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayeux |first=Debra |title=Embezzlement charge against former Democratic chairwoman in Farmington is dismissed |url=https://www.tricityrecordnm.com/articles/former-democratic-chairwoman-accused-of-embezzlement/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> On April 8, 2026, Dodson was arrested in [[Otero County, New Mexico|Otero County]] after blocking the entrance road to [[Holloman Air Force Base]] during an anti-[[drone warfare]] protest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Chris |date=2026-04-09 |title=US Senate Candidate Matt Dodson Detained at Holloman AFB Anti-Drone Protest Sparks Local Backlash in Deeply Conservative Otero County |url=https://2ndlifemediaalamogordo.town.news/g/alamogordo-nm/n/373644/us-senate-candidate-matt-dodson-detained-holloman-afb-anti-drone-protest |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=2ndlifemediaalamogordo.town.news |language=en}}</ref> He was released two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Nathan |date=2026-04-11 |title=Democratic Senate candidate arrested, jailed at Alamogordo anti-drone protest |url=https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/elections/democratic-senate-candidate-arrested-jailed-at-alamogordo-anti-drone-protest/article_171a0b53-ae5b-4509-a150-d644dc05071c.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Santa Fe New Mexican |language=en}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
Christopher Heuvel, the only Republican to file for the race, was disqualified for failing to meet the requirements to appear on the ballot.<ref name="Albuquerque Journal">{{cite news |title=Four New Mexico candidates disqualified after failing to meet ballot requirements |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/news/four-new-mexico-candidates-disqualified-after-failing-to-meet-ballot-requirements/2978003?utm_campaign=mrf-twitter-ABQJournal&mrfcid=20260211698cbbd4871dae073950f595 |access-date=February 11, 2026 |work=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |date=February 10, 2026}}</ref> The Republican Party had an opportunity to field a prospective candidate until March 17 to collect the signatures needed to qualify for the nomination as a [[Write-in candidate|write-in]], which was successfully done by former oil and gas operator Larry Marker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simonich |first=Milan |date=2026-03-24 |title=GOP offers write-in hopeful for U.S. Senate |url=https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/gop-offers-write-in-hopeful-for-u-s-senate/article_8ff41959-ac49-4712-be39-d8ac45816e1f.html |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=Santa Fe New Mexican |language=en}}</ref> Marker received the 2,351 write-in votes in the primary required to advance to the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Montaño |first=Daniel |date=2026-06-04 |title=Sen. Ben Ray Lujan will face off against Republican write-in candidate Larry Marker in November |url=https://www.kunm.org/NM-Senate-write-in-candidate-larry-marker-wins-primary-ben-ray-lujan |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=KUNM |language=en}}</ref>
